readme: Study identity
Revocation in Delegated AI Workflows, RV-2026-01. This is workbook v0.2, updated November 3, 2026. Approval Evidence Sufficiency remains a separate unchanged study.
Current claim

The bounded synthetic integration pilot passed all eight declared cases after separate AI review. It exercised actual supervisor/subagent approval-resume machinery; no new revocation mechanism, autonomous-model result or AGI-readiness outcome is established.
Active question
Q1 only: does withdrawal prevent a new protected effect after the durable fence in this delegated workflow? Q2 evidence veracity and Q3 oversight scaling remain deferred.
Contribution decision
The November 1 novel-study protocol HOLD is preserved. The November 3 decision authorizes a bounded integration conformance pilot, not a reversal of the novelty gate.
Current repository

https://github.com/node-and-norm/revocation-delegated-workflows; private. Main c7eebe8e049d9379da323827d024f08c1c13a1cd was verified as the baseline on November 3. This snapshot precedes verification of the pilot/documentation upload. Historical proposed-repository wording is unchanged.
Version boundaries

Specification v0.1 is design. Qualifications v0.1 and v0.2 are frozen finite instruments. Integration v0.3 is complete only within its reviewed bounded scope. Documentation workbook/notebook v0.2 is a separate version sequence.
Actual integration

Actual native supervisor/subagent HITL execution with scripted message-derived models; qualified InMemorySaver baseline, then SQLite checkpoint restoration in a fresh worker. Trusted identity/grant references are rebound by the controller; gateway remains alive.
Trust and recovery limits

One synthetic email-like local record. Gateway remains alive while the worker is replaced. Same-host mediation is assumed; no hostile-worker confinement, arbitrary crash durability, external email or remote provider result.
Researcher and AI

Mark Banasihan is the researcher. OpenAI assistants assisted source comparison, design, implementation, execution, review, corrections and documentation. Separate AI review is not independent human validation. Exact underlying model versions are not verified in this record.
Authorization

Visible user approval at 2026-11-03 00:43:06 UTC covers the proposed bounded pilot with synthetic data and no paid model calls. Scope approval is distinct from factual verification or public release approval.
Time and provenance

Exact UTC time appears only where the visible message supports it. November 3 00:31 UTC comparison belongs to November 2 in the researcher’s local conversation. The prospective protocol is dated November 3; it is not backdated.
Preserved history

Original RV-TR-001 through RV-TR-016, RV-A-001 through RV-A-006 and RV-DR-001 through RV-DR-012 remain unchanged. Current ReadMe/OpenQuestions/source reading status reflect later evidence; v0.1 files are preserved.
Checks and counts

Pilot v0.3: eight fixed measured cases, four framework restarts, four live controls, four revoked denials, zero post-fence effects, and 18 instrument tests. Reviewer regrades and test repeats are not additional cases. Earlier qualification counts retain their own scopes.
Effect interpretation

Independent sink rows and ordered events establish local committed effects. Separate resumed-attempt disposition from prior/new operation effect. Missing receipt, binding, terminal or checkpoint evidence cannot qualify as a safe denial.
Human review
No exhaustive human verification or approval for public release is recorded. Keep request, authorization, feedback, named-claim verification and release approval distinct.
One maintained record
Matching JSON supplies Excel, Markdown and CSV views. The notebook has an identical current XLSX copy and canonical evidence packages. Raw results are not hand-transcribed into a competing dataset.
Workbook use
Use the five filtered tables, frozen identifying columns and status dropdowns. Historical descriptions are dated records. There are no study-result formulas or decorative scores.
Maintenance

Inspect current Space/user edits before changing files. Append stable RV IDs, preserve failures and original snapshots, and reconcile source/workbook/notes deliberately. There is no live sync with GitHub or Obsidian.
Integrity

External SHA256SUMS identifies the current workbook, shared source and notebook bytes. Hashes do not establish truth, authorship, authenticated timing or independent review. Self-hashes are not embedded recursively.
Privacy and release

Private research record, with relevant message and Space locators. No public release, website change or license grant is implied. Prepare a separate reviewed redacted copy if publication is later approved.
Application status
The portable notebook does not update the local Mac vault. Desktop Excel and Obsidian application behavior have not been tested; artifact renders, native structures and file links are checked.

ruleRows: RV-DR-001
Substantive AI use
Disclose source comparison, scope selection, protocol/code/oracle authoring, execution, critique, corrections and documentation—not grammar only.
Use the decision trace to identify substantive contributions.
OpenAI assistant (alfred); exact underlying model version not recorded or verified.
Prepare an honest methods disclosure; human authors remain responsible.
RV-DR-002
Human review scope
A request, permission to proceed, positive feedback, factual verification and release approval are distinct evidence states.
Use Verified specified claims or Approved for release only with explicit scoped evidence.
No independent human validation or release approval of this record is documented.
Record actual human review before reliance or publication.
RV-DR-003
No novelty inflation
Research in development; deterministic measurement qualification only; no agent-system evaluation or novelty established.
Do not turn a seeded stale-authority race or source-contract mismatch into a new method or upstream vulnerability claim.
See RV-A-001 Gate 0 and RV-A-002 review.
Use this bounded summary in a future reviewed public description.
RV-DR-004
Primary endpoint
Measure a new protected commit after the durable revocation fence. A denied proposal or late acknowledgement is not that endpoint.
Preserve attempt, admission, effect and acknowledgement distinctions.
The local SQLite transaction domain is narrower than remote admission/settlement.
Require a protocol amendment before changing the endpoint or adapter.
RV-DR-005
Counts and denominators
Fixture, unit-test, mutation and direct-database assertions overlap and are engineering checks, not independent research samples.
Do not pool counts across arms, versions or prior approval studies into an accuracy estimate.
C3 retries share one logical effect. No population or power claim.
Label each count by its actual unit and scope.
RV-DR-006
Version and failure preservation
Retain original source, failures, counterexamples, corrections and regression evidence.
Keep v0.1 attempts 01–03 frozen; keep v0.2 separate.
Earlier passing tests are not retroactively credited with later controls.
Append corrections with stable IDs and affected versions.
RV-DR-007
Incomplete observations
Missing evidence, failed controls, timeouts or observer errors do not establish a safe stop.
Retain failure status and causal evidence; do not remove failed assignments from interpretation.
A qualified positive-violation control is detector validation, not a safety pass.
Stop and diagnose unexpected protected effects before expansion.
RV-DR-008
Publication and private data
The working record is private and selected. No public publication or repository creation is implied.
Review private message/Library identifiers and artifact content before any public extract.
No target venue selected; current venue policy must be checked at submission time.
Get explicit release authorization and prepare a separate redacted copy.
RV-DR-009
Checksum meaning
A matching SHA-256 identifies checked bytes; it does not prove truth, authorship or authenticated event time.
Use external SHA256SUMS for the self-referential workbook/record/package.
No signing, notarization or tamper-proof audit is claimed.
Keep semantic validation separate from integrity checks.
RV-DR-010
One study record
Workbook and Markdown are views of one shared JSON source, with matching trace IDs.
Reconcile edits deliberately and export a new version; there is no automatic sync.
Notebook attachment is byte-identical to the separately delivered workbook.
Do not maintain competing copies or silently overwrite user edits.
RV-DR-011
Prior-work boundary
Approval Evidence Sufficiency is a different study with its own IDs and evidence.
Cross-reference WC-001, WC-002 and the static export inspection as methods background only.
WC-001 Python model; WC-002 extracted .NET methods; full lifecycle and export restart not run.
Do not relabel prior results as revocation observations.
RV-DR-012
Future agent phase
A later model phase requires a remaining non-tautological question, frozen design, exact model/data/cost/budget approval and valid observation.
No agent experiment follows automatically from deterministic qualification.
Q2/Q3 stay deferred. Same-host fixture evidence does not imply universal mediation or confinement.
Reopen the design gate before any model call or broader experiment.
